title: Worst to First: Sonny's Ben Dover Climbs Out of the Basement and Wins Buckaroo Bowl III
dek: Two straight last-place finishes, then a 13-3 season and a title: the commissioner wrote the comeback story of the league's young history, while Kai's season ended at the bottom of the ladder despite the year's biggest week.
body: Year three of the Buckaroo Football League started with a draft that had more logistical drama than a playoff overtime. Mekhi made his picks from basic training, which is a little like filling out a bracket during a fire drill. Everyone else had a couch and a cheat sheet. By the end of the year the draft board barely resembled the final standings, and that was before the league did something it had never done before.

It traded. After two full seasons of zero deals, 2025 produced four, which in this league counts as a full-blown market boom. Nobody was going to accuse these managers of panic-selling in their first two years. But the ice finally broke, rosters finally moved, and the trade button on ESPN finally got pressed by someone other than a stray thumb.

The story of the regular season was Sonny, and it was not close. Ben Dover went 13-3, scored 1,850.8 points, and grabbed the No. 1 seed. This is the same franchise that finished dead last in 2023 and 2024, and somehow it now played like the team everyone else was measuring against. The commissioner has spent two years hearing jokes about running a league he couldn't win, and he answered with the best record the league has ever seen. Maybe Boston is rubbing off on him: suddenly the guy expects to win every week.

The cruelest numbers belonged to Kaushal. The Habibsters scored a league-best 1,973.6 points, more than 120 clear of the champion, and finished 8-8. The two-time champ spent the whole year putting up big totals and watching opponents pick that exact week to have their own big game. Randy went the other way: The fumblers scored 1,792.1, fourth-most in the league, and turned it into a 9-7 record and the No. 2 seed, the most efficient season of anyone not named Sonny.

The playoffs flipped the script on Habibi again. Randy's The fumblers ran the Habibsters off the field 137.1 to 79.96, a blowout that left the league's top scorer watching from the stands. That set up Buckaroo Bowl III between the top two seeds, and Ben Dover finished the job 105.1 to 86.48. Randy made his first Bowl and earned a well-deserved silver. Sonny got the trophy, a full rebrand of his place in league history, and permanent bragging rights over anyone who mocked those last-place finishes.

Then there was the strangest subplot in league history. Ramon ran Araleasers through Week 8, a stretch that included the season's lowest score, a 61.4 in Week 3, before getting removed for inactivity. The team became Ramon's Remains, won its very first game without him 94.76 to 92.02 over Alan, and played out the string. It finished 5-11 and fifth, and every one of those post-Brucie results sits on his record with an asterisk, which is the fantasy version of getting credit for a group project you skipped.

At the bottom, the consolation ladder picked an unlikely victim. Mekhi's Dawgs went 8-8, scored 1,858.2 points, more than the champion, and owned the single biggest week of the season, a 153.62 in Week 9. They still ended up sixth after a fourth-seed finish slid all the way down the ladder, while Alan's Team Pillbert rode the ladder up from the sixth seed to fourth place. It was a reminder that this game punishes even the best football minds. Next year the league grows to eight teams, Kai gets his shot at revenge, and for the first time ever, the guy holding the trophy is the guy who built the league.
